# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, or remove an English sentence the Korean does not support.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Keep every `> **System**` panel from the mastered chapter, including a notice the narrator only hears. Do not turn a panel into italics, a sound effect, or narration. Do not repeat a panel. A notice the mastered chapter already shows more than once stays repeated that many times, and no more. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks. Keep a mastered thought in italics. Do not turn it into spoken dialogue.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

아직 만나지 못한 진태경 주니어.

그리고 어쩌면 영원히 만나지 못할 2세의 모습이다.

아기의 천진난만한 눈망울이 내게 물었다.

- 아빠, 나 못 나와?

한 번, 두 번, 세 번. 신체 내부에서 굉음과 진동이 천둥처럼 울려 퍼졌다.

부릅뜬 눈에서 실핏줄이 터져 나갔다.

이어 이미 임맥을 두드리고 있던 영약의 기운과 적천강의 공력에 합세한다.

세 기운이 한데 뭉친 공성추가 그 어느 때보다 힘차고 날카롭게 성문을 강타했다.

그건 종지부였다. 길었던 힘겨루기의 끝을 알리는.

굳게 막혀 있던 임맥이 허물어지고 기운들이 점령군처럼 들이닥쳤다.

순간 아찔해질 정도의 고통, 그리고 내가 느낀 고통의 몇 배는 됨직한 쾌감과 청량감이 전신을 휩쓸었다.

띠링.



- [임맥]을 성공적으로 타통 했습니다!

- 기의 수발이 한층 자유로워집니다!

- 공력을 순환, 축적하는 속도가 비약적으로 상승합니다!

- 업적, [임맥 타통]을 달성하셨습니다!

- 보상으로…….



‘아아, 아아아!’

이제는 고통이 아닌 환희로 몸이 떨렸다. 다르다. 내가 지금까지 알고 있었던 것은 모두 새 발의 피였다.

그것은 일류와 절정만큼이나 엄청난 차이였다.

‘이렇게 달라질 수 있다니.’

비록 엄청난 고통을 겪어야 했지만 이런 성취라면 감수할 만하다. 아니, 반드시 참아야 한다.

놀라워하는 내게 적천강이 활짝 웃어 보였다.

“정말 잘했다!”

진심으로 기뻐하는 그의 모습에 가슴 한구석이 뭉클해졌다.

이렇게까지 힘껏 도와줄 줄이야. 점혈 된 상태가 아니었다면 적천강에게 큰절이라도 올렸을 것이다.

‘적천강, 당신은 도대체.’

눈가가 촉촉해지던 그때였다.

“독맥(督脈)도 이렇게 하면 충분히 뚫을 수 있다.”

“…….”

아니, 시벌.

저걸 깜빡했네.

‘이걸 한 번 더 하라고?’

안 돼. 안 해! 최소한 잠깐 쉬었다가 해!

필사적으로 눈을 깜빡이는 나를 보며 적천강이 허허 웃었다.

“……!”

그렇게 지옥행 급행열차가 다시 출발했고, 한 시진 뒤 나는 혼미해진 정신 너머로 희미한 시스템 알림을 들을 수 있었다.

띠링.



- [독맥]을 타통 했습니다!

- 퀘스트, [임독양맥]을 성공적으로 완료했습니다!

- 희귀한 업적을 달성했습니다! 보상으로……

.

.

.



몰라, 시바.

희귀한 업적이고 나발이고, 더 이상은 못 버티겠다.

모든 정신력을 소모한 나는 끝이 보이지 않는 암흑 속으로 곤두박질쳤다.



* * *



스르륵.

밧줄을 풀자마자 무너지는 진태경의 신형을, 적천강은 조심히 감싸 안았다. 고통을 참느라 흘린 땀과 앞서 배출한 탁기로 악취가 진동했지만 아무래도 상관없었다.

그것들은 더 높은 경지에 오르기 위해 노력한 무인의 흔적이다.

혼절한 진태경을 바라보는 적천강의 눈빛은 그 어느 때보다 깊었고, 온화했다.

‘알면 알수록 대단한 녀석이다.’

처음에는 그런 생각도 했다.

왜 하필 이 녀석이었을까, 하는 생각.

그의 눈에 비친 진태경은 백색도 흑색도 아니었다. 세상 어디에서나 찾아볼 수 있는 회색이 바로 녀석이었다.

딱히 정의감에 불타지도, 그렇다고 악하지도 않은.

‘그렇다고 무공 수련에 열심인 녀석도 아니었지.’

태원진가에 온 직후 진태경에 관한 말들은 귀에 못 박히도록 들었다.

굳이 물어보지 않아도 주위에서 항상 떠들어 댔다.

무공은 삼류에, 주색잡기는 일류. 뛰어난 재능을 가진 두 형과는 달리 가문의 수치라 불렸다고 했다.

적천강은 그 사실을 알고 잠시나마 하늘을 원망했다.

Humans were imperfect beings to begin with. Trying to divide them into perfect white and black was absurd.

Perhaps gray was merely another name for a good person.

It must have been unbearably difficult and painful. Even so, he had endured through sheer determination to become stronger.

Jin Taekyung possessed a mental strength as firm as his physique.

“Not yet, you bastard. Hold out for just a few more years.”

Jeok Cheongang muttered bitterly and lifted Jin Taekyung into his arms.

They had crossed a great mountain. Now it was time to rest.

For the young man and the old man alike.

When he opened the door and entered, Jin Wikyung, who had been scribbling something across a bamboo slip, brightened and rose from his seat.

“Sir Ak, welcome. Thank you for accepting my invitation despite how busy you must be.”

“It only makes sense for the man with more time on his hands to make the trip. Please don’t concern yourself with it.”

The Shandong Yue Family was renowned throughout the Murim as a prestigious family of spear masters.

Yet despite being a direct descendant of such an illustrious family, Ak Bulgun was a straightforward man with little patience for empty formalities.

That personality showed plainly when he got straight to the point without even pausing for a sip of tea.

“Why did you summon me? Could it be…”

Jin Wikyung smiled faintly.

“Unfortunately, this isn’t about Mukyung.”

“I see.”

Ak Bulgun nodded, then added bluntly,

“Lesser Family Head, please understand that Heaven’s Gate Temple enforces its rules strictly.”

Anyone with sufficient talent could become a cadet regardless of their background. Its members consequently ranged from disciples of small sects in remote regions to the disciples and scions of prestigious major sects.

Despite bringing together people from such disparate backgrounds, Heaven’s Gate Temple had avoided serious conflict by enforcing the same strict rules upon every cadet.

“If he fails to return by the appointed date, he may be expelled. Even the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are no exception.”

“I did go to see him myself, but…”

“Did he refuse?”

“Yes.”

According to Childeuk, the martial artist stationed at the training hall, Mukyung hadn’t stepped outside once since entering.

“I won’t return until I achieve Great Completion.”

Ak Bulgun let out a short laugh after hearing Jin Wikyung’s explanation.

Having taught Jin Mukyung several times before, he knew the young genius’s personality well.

“That sounds like him.”

“It’s unfortunate, but I don’t think even I can overcome my little brother’s stubbornness.”

“The Temple Master will be just as disappointed as you are, Lesser Family Head.”

“I don’t believe I’ve heard why you asked to see me.”

“Ah, I wanted to deliver a message to you.”

“A message?”

Instead of answering, Jin Wikyung drew a small bamboo tube from inside his robe and handed it over.

Ak Bulgun examined the characters engraved into the blue bamboo tube and murmured,

“Heaven’s Gate Temple?”

“It arrived half a shichen ago. I thought it best to bring you here so I could hand it over personally.”

“Please excuse me for a moment.”

After asking permission, Ak Bulgun silently read through the message.

He checked it twice, then a third time, before raising his head and staring at Jin Wikyung.

“Lesser Family Head.”

“……?”

“I’m going to need your help.”

[^1]: A *shichen* is a traditional Chinese time unit of approximately two hours.

A tremendous surge of internal energy began racing along the path.

Opening the Conception Vessel required passing through a pathway of twenty-four acupoints, beginning with the Huiyin Acupoint.

*Oh, my baby!*

Jin Taekyung Junior, whom I had yet to meet.

The child I might now never meet at all.

The baby’s innocent eyes seemed to ask me:

“Daddy, can’t I come out?”

*Kyaaaaaaah!*

*I can’t die like this!*

*Hng!*

And finally…

Boom!

The difference was that this collision didn’t end with a single blow.

Boom! Boom! Boom!

Once. Twice. Three times.

Once, twice, three times. Thunderous booms and vibrations rang out inside my body like thunder from the heavens.

Only then did I understand why Jeok Cheongang had pressed my Paralysis Acupoint and Mute Acupoint. And why he had secured me with ropes on top of that.

*Gnnngh!*

Pop.

That blow put an end to it.

Ding.

> - The handling of qi has become much freer!
>
> - Your speed of circulating and accumulating internal energy has increased dramatically!

> - As a reward…

*How can it change this much?*

I’d suffered unimaginable pain, but an achievement like this was worth it. No—I had to endure it.

“You did very well!”

*Jeok Cheongang, you really…*

“We can open the Governor Vessel the same way.”

*He wants me to do this all over again?*

“……!”

> - Quest **Conception and Governor Vessels** was completed successfully!
>
> - You have achieved a rare Achievement! As a reward…

.

.

.

The sweat Taekyung had shed while enduring the pain and the turbid qi expelled from his body earlier combined into a terrible stench, but Jeok Cheongang didn’t care.

They were the traces left by a martial artist striving to reach a higher realm.

Jeok Cheongang gazed down at the unconscious Jin Taekyung with eyes deeper and gentler than ever.

*The more I learn about him, the more remarkable he becomes.*

*Why him, of all people?*

He wasn’t exactly burning with a sense of justice, but neither was he evil.

*Nor was he particularly devoted to training in martial arts.*

From the moment Jeok Cheongang arrived at the Jin Family of Taiyuan, he’d heard about Jin Taekyung until his ears ached.

He hadn’t even needed to ask. Everyone around him was always talking about the boy.

His martial arts were Third Rate, while his drinking, womanizing, and gambling were First Rate. Unlike his two gifted older brothers, he had been called a disgrace to the family.

Upon learning that, Jeok Cheongang had resented the heavens, if only for a moment.

*Why did you give the Heavenly Martial Physique to someone like him?*

A fine sword ought to belong to a swordsman, not a farmer.

Yet the Jin Taekyung of the rumors was no different from a farmer holding a fine sword. Worse, he didn’t even possess a farmer’s diligence.

The only pursuits he approached diligently were drinking, womanizing, and gambling. What more was there to say?

But…

*I was wrong.*

Looking back, Jeok Cheongang realized that everything he had thought was merely an old man’s stubborn prejudice and contradiction.

He was no immortal sage. How could he divide someone he’d only just met into black or white? And what did it matter if Taekyung was gray?

*A human heart. As long as he keeps hold of that, it is enough.*

Judging by everything Jeok Cheongang had seen so far, Jin Taekyung was a decent young man.

Humans were imperfect beings to begin with. Trying to divide them into perfect white and black was absurd.

Perhaps gray was merely another name for a good person.

*And on top of that, he possesses remarkable mental strength.*

What good was being born with a fine physique? Opening the Conception and Governor Vessels was so difficult and agonizing that the process could only be called hellish.

Yet Jin Taekyung had done it—and done it splendidly.

It must have been unbearably difficult and painful. Even so, he had endured through sheer determination to become stronger.

Jin Taekyung possessed a mental strength as firm as his physique.

*The Heavenly Martial Physique chose its master well.*

A satisfied smile appeared around Jeok Cheongang’s mouth. After gazing at Jin Taekyung for a long while, he muttered:

“Perhaps… it may happen much sooner than I thought.”

As soon as he finished speaking, Jeok Cheongang’s wrinkled fingers began to tremble.

Even for him, the process had consumed a considerable amount of internal energy and mental strength. Before his mind could fully register the toll, his aging body had already made it clear.

“Not yet, you bastard. Hold out for just a few more years.”

Jeok Cheongang muttered bitterly and lifted Jin Taekyung into his arms.

They had crossed a great mountain. Now it was time to rest.

For the young man and the old man alike.

* * *

It was around noon when Ak Bulgun, a spear instructor at Heaven’s Gate Temple, arrived at Jin Wikyung’s office.

When he opened the door and entered, Jin Wikyung, who had been scribbling something across a bamboo slip, brightened and rose from his seat.

“Sir Ak, welcome. Thank you for accepting my invitation despite how busy you must be.”

“It only makes sense for the man with more time on his hands to make the trip. Please don’t concern yourself with it.”

The Shandong Yue Family was renowned throughout the Murim as a prestigious family of spear masters.

Yet despite being a direct descendant of such an illustrious family, Ak Bulgun was a straightforward man with little patience for empty formalities.

That personality showed plainly when he got straight to the point without even pausing for a sip of tea.

“Why did you summon me? Could it be…”

Jin Wikyung smiled faintly.

“Unfortunately, this isn’t about Mukyung.”

“I see.”

Ak Bulgun nodded, then added bluntly,

“Lesser Family Head, please understand that Heaven’s Gate Temple enforces its rules strictly.”

Heaven’s Gate Temple was both a treasure trove of outstanding talent and a gateway to advancement.

Anyone with sufficient talent could become a cadet regardless of their background. Its members consequently ranged from disciples of small sects in remote regions to the disciples and scions of prestigious major sects.

Despite bringing together people from such disparate backgrounds, Heaven’s Gate Temple had avoided serious conflict by enforcing the same strict rules upon every cadet.

“If he fails to return by the appointed date, he may be expelled. Even the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are no exception.”

“I did go to see him myself, but…”

“Did he refuse?”

“Yes.”

After much deliberation, Jin Wikyung had gone to see him, but Jin Mukyung hadn’t even shown his face.

According to Childeuk, the martial artist stationed at the training hall, Mukyung hadn’t stepped outside once since entering.

He subsisted on fasting pills and refused to let anyone approach him. At least, when he heard that Jin Wikyung had come, he sent back a brief answer:

“I won’t return until I achieve Great Completion.”

Ak Bulgun let out a short laugh after hearing Jin Wikyung’s explanation.

Having taught Jin Mukyung several times before, he knew the young genius’s personality well.

“That sounds like him.”

“It’s unfortunate, but I don’t think even I can overcome my little brother’s stubbornness.”

“The Temple Master will be just as disappointed as you are, Lesser Family Head.”

Everyone had their own path to follow. Ak Bulgun nodded matter-of-factly and continued.

“I don’t believe I’ve heard why you asked to see me.”

“Ah, I wanted to deliver a message to you.”

“A message?”

Instead of answering, Jin Wikyung drew a small bamboo tube from inside his robe and handed it over.

Ak Bulgun examined the characters engraved into the blue bamboo tube and murmured,

“Heaven’s Gate Temple?”

“It arrived half a shichen ago. I thought it best to bring you here so I could hand it over personally.”

“Please excuse me for a moment.”

After asking permission, Ak Bulgun silently read through the message.

He checked it twice, then a third time, before raising his head and staring at Jin Wikyung.

“Lesser Family Head.”

“……?”

“I’m going to need your help.”

[^1]: A *shichen* is a traditional Chinese time unit of approximately two hours.

The moment Jeok Cheongang loosened the ropes, Jin Taekyung’s collapsing body fell into his careful embrace.

The sweat Taekyung had shed while enduring the pain and the turbid qi expelled from his body earlier combined into a terrible stench, but Jeok Cheongang didn’t care.

They were the traces left by a martial artist striving to reach a higher realm.

Jeok Cheongang gazed down at the unconscious Jin Taekyung with eyes deeper and gentler than ever.

*The more I learn about him, the more remarkable he becomes.*

At first, Jeok Cheongang had wondered one thing.

*Why him, of all people?*

In his eyes, Jin Taekyung had been neither white nor black. He was gray—the same ordinary gray found everywhere in the world.

He wasn’t exactly burning with a sense of justice, but neither was he evil.

*Nor was he particularly devoted to training in martial arts.*

From the moment Jeok Cheongang arrived at the Jin Family of Taiyuan, he’d heard about Jin Taekyung until his ears ached.

He hadn’t even needed to ask. Everyone around him was always talking about the boy.

His martial arts were Third Rate, while his drinking, womanizing, and gambling were First Rate. Unlike his two gifted older brothers, he had been called a disgrace to the family.

Upon learning that, Jeok Cheongang had resented the heavens, if only for a moment.

*Why did you give the Heavenly Martial Physique to someone like him?*

A fine sword ought to belong to a swordsman, not a farmer.

Yet the Jin Taekyung of the rumors was no different from a farmer holding a fine sword. Worse, he didn’t even possess a farmer’s diligence.

The only pursuits he approached diligently were drinking, womanizing, and gambling. What more was there to say?

But…

*I was wrong.*

Looking back, Jeok Cheongang realized that everything he had thought was merely an old man’s stubborn prejudice and contradiction.

He was no immortal sage. How could he divide someone he’d only just met into black or white? And what did it matter if Taekyung was gray?

*A human heart. As long as he keeps hold of that, it is enough.*

Judging by everything Jeok Cheongang had seen so far, Jin Taekyung was a decent young man.

Humans were imperfect beings to begin with. Trying to divide them into perfect white and black was absurd.

Perhaps gray was merely another name for a good person.

*And on top of that, he possesses remarkable mental strength.*

What good was being born with a fine physique? Opening the Conception and Governor Vessels was so difficult and agonizing that the process could only be called hellish.

Yet Jin Taekyung had done it—and done it splendidly.

It must have been unbearably difficult and painful. Even so, he had endured through sheer determination to become stronger.

Jin Taekyung possessed a mental strength as firm as his physique.

*The Heavenly Martial Physique chose its master well.*

A satisfied smile appeared around Jeok Cheongang’s mouth. After gazing at Jin Taekyung for a long while, he muttered:

“Perhaps… it may happen much sooner than I thought.”

As soon as he finished speaking, Jeok Cheongang’s wrinkled fingers began to tremble.

Even for him, the process had consumed a considerable amount of internal energy and mental strength. Before his mind could fully register the toll, his aging body had already made it clear.

“Not yet, you bastard. Hold out for just a few more years.”

Jeok Cheongang muttered bitterly and lifted Jin Taekyung into his arms.

They had crossed a great mountain. Now it was time to rest.

For the young man and the old man alike.

It was around noon when Ak Bulgun, a spear instructor at Heaven’s Gate Temple, arrived at Jin Wikyung’s office.

When he opened the door and entered, Jin Wikyung, who had been scribbling something across a bamboo slip, brightened and rose from his seat.

“Sir Ak, welcome. Thank you for accepting my invitation despite how busy you must be.”

“It only makes sense for the man with more time on his hands to make the trip. Please don’t concern yourself with it.”

The Shandong Yue Family was renowned throughout the Murim as a prestigious family of spear masters.

Yet despite being a direct descendant of such an illustrious family, Ak Bulgun was a straightforward man with little patience for empty formalities.

That personality showed plainly when he got straight to the point without even pausing for a sip of tea.

“Why did you summon me? Could it be…”

Jin Wikyung smiled faintly.

“Unfortunately, this isn’t about Mukyung.”

“I see.”

Ak Bulgun nodded, then added bluntly,

“Lesser Family Head, please understand that Heaven’s Gate Temple enforces its rules strictly.”

Heaven’s Gate Temple was both a treasure trove of outstanding talent and a gateway to advancement.

Anyone with sufficient talent could become a cadet regardless of their background. Its members consequently ranged from disciples of small sects in remote regions to the disciples and scions of prestigious major sects.

Despite bringing together people from such disparate backgrounds, Heaven’s Gate Temple had avoided serious conflict by enforcing the same strict rules upon every cadet.

“If he fails to return by the appointed date, he may be expelled. Even the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are no exception.”

“I did go to see him myself, but…”

“Did he refuse?”

“Yes.”

After much deliberation, Jin Wikyung had gone to see him, but Jin Mukyung hadn’t even shown his face.

According to Childeuk, the martial artist stationed at the training hall, Mukyung hadn’t stepped outside once since entering.

He subsisted on fasting pills and refused to let anyone approach him. At least, when he heard that Jin Wikyung had come, he sent back a brief answer:

“I won’t return until I achieve Great Completion.”

Ak Bulgun let out a short laugh after hearing Jin Wikyung’s explanation.

Having taught Jin Mukyung several times before, he knew the young genius’s personality well.

“That sounds like him.”

“It’s unfortunate, but I don’t think even I can overcome my little brother’s stubbornness.”

“The Temple Master will be just as disappointed as you are, Lesser Family Head.”

Everyone had their own path to follow. Ak Bulgun nodded matter-of-factly and continued.

“I don’t believe I’ve heard why you asked to see me.”

“Ah, I wanted to deliver a message to you.”

“A message?”

Instead of answering, Jin Wikyung drew a small bamboo tube from inside his robe and handed it over.

Ak Bulgun examined the characters engraved into the blue bamboo tube and murmured,

“Heaven’s Gate Temple?”

“It arrived half a shichen ago.[^1] I thought it best to bring you here so I could hand it over personally.”

“Please excuse me for a moment.”

After asking permission, Ak Bulgun silently read through the message.

He checked it twice, then a third time, before raising his head and staring at Jin Wikyung.

“Lesser Family Head.”

“……?”

“I’m going to need your help.”

[^1]: A *shichen* is a traditional Chinese time unit of approximately two hours; half a shichen is approximately one hour.
